# Mintlify Starter Kit

Source: https://github.com/sajn-se/sajn-docs/blob/main/README.md

# Mintlify Starter Kit

Use the starter kit to get your docs deployed and ready to customize.

Click the green **Use this template** button at the top of this repo to copy the Mintlify starter kit. The starter kit contains examples with

- Guide pages
- Navigation
- Customizations
- API reference pages
- Use of popular components

**[Follow the full quickstart guide](https://starter.mintlify.com/quickstart)**

## Development

Install the [Mintlify CLI](https://www.npmjs.com/package/mint) to preview your documentation changes locally. To install, use the following command:

```
npm i -g mint
```

Run the following command at the root of your documentation, where your `docs.json` is located:

```
mint dev
```

View your local preview at `http://localhost:3000`.

## Publishing changes

Install our GitHub app from your [dashboard](https://dashboard.mintlify.com/settings/organization/github-app) to propagate changes from your repo to your deployment. Changes are deployed to production automatically after pushing to the default branch.

## Need help?

### Troubleshooting

- If your dev environment isn't running: Run `mint update` to ensure you have the most recent version of the CLI.
- If a page loads as a 404: Make sure you are running in a folder with a valid `docs.json`.

### Resources
- [Mintlify documentation](https://mintlify.com/docs)

---

# Authentication

Source: https://github.com/sajn-se/sajn-docs/blob/main/authentication.mdx

title: Authentication
description: 'Learn how to authenticate with the sajn API'

# Authentication

The sajn API uses API keys to authenticate requests. All API requests must include your API key in the `Authorization` header.

## Getting Your API Key

1. Log in to your sajn account at [app.sajn.se](https://app.sajn.se)
2. Navigate to **Organization Settings** > **API Keys**
3. Click **Create API Key**
4. Copy your API key and store it securely

<Warning>
  Never share your API key or commit it to version control. Treat it like a password.
</Warning>

## Making Authenticated Requests

Include your API key in the `Authorization` header as a Bearer token:

```bash
curl https://app.sajn.se/api/v1/documents \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"
```

### Example with Different Languages

<CodeGroup>

```javascript Node.js
const axios = require('axios');

const response = await axios.get('https://app.sajn.se/api/v1/documents', {
  headers: {
    'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.SAJN_API_KEY}`
  }
});
```

```python Python
import requests

response = requests.get(
    'https://app.sajn.se/api/v1/documents',
    headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {os.environ["SAJN_API_KEY"]}'}
)
```

```php PHP
<?php
$ch = curl_init('https://app.sajn.se/api/v1/documents');
curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER, [
    'Authorization: Bearer ' . getenv('SAJN_API_KEY')
]);
$response = curl_exec($ch);
```

```go Go
package main

import (
    "net/http"
    "os"
)

func main() {
    client := &http.Client{}
    req, _ := http.NewRequest("GET", "https://app.sajn.se/api/v1/documents", nil)
    req.Header.Add("Authorization", "Bearer " + os.Getenv("SAJN_API_KEY"))
    resp, _ := client.Do(req)
}
```

</CodeGroup>

## API Key Security Best Practices

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Store securely">
    Store API keys in environment variables or secure credential management systems, never in code.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Rotate regularly">
    Rotate your API keys periodically to minimize the impact of potential compromises.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Use separate keys">
    Use different API keys for development, staging, and production environments.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Monitor usage">
    Regularly review API key usage in your sajn dashboard to detect unauthorized access.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Error Responses

If authentication fails, you'll receive a `401 Unauthorized` response:

```json
{
  "message": "Invalid or missing API key"
}
```

Common authentication errors:

| Error | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `401 Unauthorized` | API key is missing, invalid, or expired |
| `403 Forbidden` | API key doesn't have permission for this resource |

## Rate Limiting

API requests are rate limited per API key:

- **100 requests per minute**
- **1000 requests per hour**

Rate limit information is included in response headers:

```
X-RateLimit-Limit: 100
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 95
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1640000000
```

When you exceed the rate limit, you'll receive a `429 Too Many Requests` response.

# CLAUDE.md

Source: https://github.com/sajn-se/sajn-docs/blob/main/CLAUDE.md

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

This is a Mintlify documentation site for sajn, a digital document signing platform. The documentation includes guides, API references, and changelogs organized in a multi-tab structure.

## Local Development Commands

### Preview Documentation Locally
```bash
# Install Mintlify CLI globally (first time only)
npm i -g mint

# Start the local development server
mint dev
```
The preview will be available at `http://localhost:3000` and updates automatically as you edit files.

### Update CLI (troubleshooting)
```bash
mint update
```

## Project Structure

- **docs.json**: Central configuration file defining navigation, theme, colors, and OpenAPI integration
- **api/openapi.json**: OpenAPI specification that auto-generates API documentation pages
- **MDX files**: Documentation content with YAML frontmatter and Mintlify components
- **Key directories**:
  - `api/`: API documentation and OpenAPI spec
  - `concepts/`, `guides/`: Conceptual and procedural documentation (referenced in docs.json but files may need creation)
  - `essentials/`: General Mintlify documentation templates
  - `changelog/`: Version history
  - `snippets/`: Reusable content blocks
  - `images/`, `logo/`: Media assets

## Navigation Architecture

The site uses a **tab-based navigation** defined in docs.json:

1. **Documentation tab**: Getting Started, Core Concepts, Guides
2. **API Reference tab**: Auto-generated from OpenAPI spec with custom groupings
3. **Changelog tab**: Version history

Navigation is controlled entirely through docs.json. When adding new pages:
1. Create the MDX file with proper frontmatter
2. Add the file path (without `.mdx` extension) to the appropriate `pages` array in docs.json
3. For API endpoints, they're auto-generated from openapi.json but must be listed in docs.json navigation

## Content Requirements

### MDX File Frontmatter (Required)
Every MDX file must include:
```yaml
---
title: "Page Title"
description: "Concise description for SEO and navigation"
---
```

### Writing Standards
- Use second-person voice ("you")
- Include prerequisites at the start of procedural content
- Test all code examples before committing
- Add language tags to all code blocks
- Use relative paths for internal links (e.g., `/quickstart` not absolute URLs)
- Match style and formatting of existing pages

### Mintlify Components
The site uses Mintlify-specific MDX components:
- `<Card>`, `<CardGroup>`: Visual navigation cards
- `<Accordion>`, `<AccordionGroup>`: Collapsible content
- `<Tip>`, `<Note>`, `<Warning>`: Callout boxes
- `<Columns>`: Multi-column layouts

## OpenAPI Integration

The API Reference tab is powered by `api/openapi.json`. When updating the API:
1. Modify the OpenAPI spec in openapi.json
2. Ensure endpoint paths match the navigation structure in docs.json
3. The format uses HTTP method + path (e.g., `"GET /api/v1/documents"`) in the navigation

## Git Workflow

- **NEVER use `--no-verify`** when committing
- Create a new branch for changes when appropriate
- Commit frequently throughout development
- Changes pushed to the default branch (main) are automatically deployed to production via Mintlify's GitHub app

## Deployment

The site is deployed automatically through the Mintlify GitHub app. After pushing to the main branch, changes propagate to production within moments. No manual deployment steps required.

## Bilingual Content Note

Some content (particularly API reference introduction) is in Swedish. Maintain language consistency when editing existing pages - don't translate unless explicitly requested.

---

# Developer MCP Server

Source: https://github.com/sajn-se/sajn-docs/blob/main/developer-mcp.mdx

title: Developer MCP Server
description: 'Connect an AI assistant to your sajn workspace to debug API logs, webhook deliveries, documents and more over the Model Context Protocol'

# Developer MCP Server

The **Developer MCP Server** lets an AI assistant act on your live sajn **workspace** — read your documents, templates and contacts, and debug your integration by inspecting **API request logs** and **outbound webhook deliveries**. It speaks the same authentication and permission model as the [REST API](/api/introduction).

<Note>
This is **not** the same as the [documentation MCP server](/docs-mcp) at `https://docs.sajn.se/mcp`. That one only searches these docs and needs no login. The Developer MCP server connects to your **real account data** and requires authentication.
</Note>

| | Documentation MCP | Developer MCP |
|---|---|---|
| **URL** | `https://docs.sajn.se/mcp` | `https://app.sajn.se/api/mcp` |
| **Auth** | None (public) | OAuth 2.0 / API key |
| **Data** | Documentation only | Your live workspace |
| **Use for** | "How do I…" questions | Debugging logs & webhooks, acting on documents |

## Server URL

```
https://app.sajn.se/api/mcp
```

The server is a stateless [Streamable HTTP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-03-26/basic/transports) endpoint — every request carries its own bearer token, so any standard remote-MCP client works.

## Authentication

The Developer MCP server is bound to a single **workspace** and enforces the same `role ∩ scope` rule as the REST API. There are two ways to authenticate:

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="OAuth (recommended)">
    Most MCP clients (Claude, Cursor, …) discover and complete OAuth automatically. When you add the server, the client opens a sajn consent screen where you pick the **workspace** and approve the **scopes** the assistant may use. Read-only access is the default — write and destructive tools only appear after you grant the matching scope.

    No tokens to copy or rotate; the client refreshes them for you.
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="API key">
    For clients that send a static `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header, you can use a workspace [API key](/authentication). The connection then has exactly the role and scopes of that key.

    To use the debugging tools, the key must carry the `audit:read` scope and belong to a member with the **Manage developer** workspace permission (see below).
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

<Warning>
The Developer MCP server requires a **paid plan**. Connections on the free plan are rejected.
</Warning>

### Scopes and permissions

Every tool requires specific OAuth scopes, and tools are **filtered to what your connection is allowed to see** — a read-only connection never even lists the write tools. The developer debugging tools additionally require the **Manage developer** workspace permission, so only developers can read raw request and webhook traffic.

| Tool group | Required scope | Required permission |
|---|---|---|
| Read documents / templates / contacts / sajn IDs | `documents:read`, `contacts:read`, … | — |
| **Debugging: API logs & webhook deliveries** | `audit:read` | Manage developer |
| Send / remind / withdraw / delete documents | `documents:write`, `documents:delete` | matching role |
| Create contacts | `contacts:write` | matching role |

## Debugging tools

These are the tools most useful for diagnosing an integration. All are read-only and require the `audit:read` scope plus the **Manage developer** permission.

### API request logs

<ResponseField name="list_api_logs" type="read-only">
  List recent v1 REST API requests for the workspace, newest first. Filter by `method` (GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE), `statusCode` (`200`/`400`/`500` for a class, or an exact code), or `search` (path or IP). Paginated (`page`, `perPage`, max 100). Returns lean rows — method, path, status, duration, time.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="get_api_log" type="read-only">
  Fetch a single API request log by `logId` (from `list_api_logs`) with its full **headers, request body and response body** — to see exactly what a client sent and what sajn returned.
</ResponseField>

### Webhook deliveries

<ResponseField name="list_webhook_deliveries" type="read-only">
  List recent outbound webhook deliveries, newest first. Filter by `webhookId`, `status` (`SUCCESS`/`FAILED`), or `search` (target URL). Paginated. Returns target URL, event, status, response code and attempt number.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="get_webhook_delivery" type="read-only">
  Fetch a single delivery by `deliveryId` (from `list_webhook_deliveries`) with its full **request headers, request body and response body** — to see exactly what sajn sent to an endpoint and how it responded.
</ResponseField>

### Other tools

Beyond debugging, the same connection exposes read tools (`whoami`, `list_documents`, `get_document`, `list_templates`, `get_template`, `search_contacts`, `list_sajn_ids`, `get_sajn_id`) and — once you grant the matching scope — write tools (`send_document`, `send_reminders`, `withdraw_document`, `delete_document`, `create_contact`). Destructive tools carry a `destructive` hint so clients can prompt before running them.

## Setup

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Claude Code">
    ```bash
    claude mcp add --transport http sajn https://app.sajn.se/api/mcp
    ```

    On first use Claude Code opens the sajn OAuth consent screen in your browser. Pick the workspace and approve the scopes. Verify with:

    ```bash
    claude mcp list
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Claude Desktop">
    1. Open **Settings** > **Connectors** > **Add Connector**
    2. Enter:
       - **Name**: sajn
       - **URL**: `https://app.sajn.se/api/mcp`
    3. Click **Save**, then complete the OAuth consent flow when prompted.
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Cursor">
    Open **Cursor Settings: Open MCP Config** and add:

    ```json
    {
      "mcpServers": {
        "sajn": {
          "url": "https://app.sajn.se/api/mcp"
        }
      }
    }
    ```

    Restart Cursor and complete the OAuth flow.
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="VS Code">
    Create `.vscode/mcp.json`:

    ```json
    {
      "servers": {
        "sajn": {
          "type": "http",
          "url": "https://app.sajn.se/api/mcp"
        }
      }
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Example prompts

Once connected, ask your assistant to debug your integration:

- "List the failed webhook deliveries from the last day and show me the response body of the first one."
- "Find the API requests that returned 4xx today and tell me what's wrong with them."
- "Get the full request and response for API log `<id>`."
- "Which webhook endpoint is failing, and what status code is it returning?"
- "Show the most recent POST requests to `/api/v1/documents` and their status codes."

## Security

- **Workspace-scoped** — a connection only ever sees data in the workspace you approved at consent.
- **Least privilege** — tools are filtered to the granted scopes; read-only by default, and the debugging tools are further gated behind the **Manage developer** permission.
- **Same enforcement as REST** — scopes and role permissions are re-checked on every tool call, not just at listing time.
- **Rate limited** — per-IP and per-organization limits apply, the same as the REST API.

## Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="The debugging tools don't show up">
    The connection must have the `audit:read` scope **and** the member must hold the **Manage developer** workspace permission. Re-run the OAuth consent and make sure `audit:read` is granted, or use an API key that has it.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Connection rejected / 401">
    - Confirm the URL is `https://app.sajn.se/api/mcp` (note `/api/mcp`, not `/mcp`).
    - The account must be on a **paid plan**.
    - For API-key auth, send the key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="Write or delete tools are missing">
    They are hidden until you grant the matching scope (`documents:write`, `documents:delete`, `contacts:write`) at consent. Reconnect and approve the additional scopes.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Next Steps

  <Card title="Authentication" icon="key" href="/authentication">
    API keys, scopes and OAuth
  <Card title="Webhooks" icon="webhook" href="/api/introduction">
    Set up and debug webhook endpoints

# Documentation MCP Server

Source: https://github.com/sajn-se/sajn-docs/blob/main/docs-mcp.mdx

title: Documentation MCP Server
description: 'Connect AI assistants to sajn documentation using the Model Context Protocol'

# Documentation MCP Server

<Note>
Looking to debug your integration (API logs, webhook deliveries) or act on your live workspace data? That's the separate [Developer MCP server](/developer-mcp) at `https://app.sajn.se/api/mcp` — this page covers the **read-only documentation** MCP only.
</Note>

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) enables AI assistants to search and retrieve information directly from sajn documentation. This provides more accurate, up-to-date responses compared to general web search.

## What is MCP?

MCP is an open protocol that standardizes how AI applications connect to external data sources. When you connect an AI assistant to sajn's MCP server, it can:

- Search our documentation directly during conversations
- Access the latest API reference and guides
- Provide accurate answers about sajn features and integration

## MCP Server URL

```
https://docs.sajn.se/mcp
```

## Setup Instructions

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Claude Desktop">
    ### Claude Desktop

    1. Open Claude Desktop
    2. Go to **Settings** > **Connectors**
    3. Click **Add Connector**
    4. Enter the following details:
       - **Name**: sajn Docs
       - **URL**: `https://docs.sajn.se/mcp`
    5. Click **Save**

    The sajn documentation is now available to Claude. You can ask questions like "How do I create a document in sajn?" and Claude will search the documentation automatically.
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Claude Code">
    ### Claude Code (CLI)

    Add the MCP server using the CLI:

    ```bash
    claude mcp add --transport http sajn-docs https://docs.sajn.se/mcp
    ```

    Verify it's connected:

    ```bash
    claude mcp list
    ```

    You can now ask Claude Code questions about sajn and it will search the documentation.
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Cursor">
    ### Cursor

    1. Open the Command Palette (`Cmd+Shift+P` on Mac, `Ctrl+Shift+P` on Windows/Linux)
    2. Search for **Cursor Settings: Open MCP Config**
    3. Add the sajn MCP server to your configuration:

    ```json
    {
      "mcpServers": {
        "sajn-docs": {
          "url": "https://docs.sajn.se/mcp"
        }
      }
    }
    ```

    4. Save the file and restart Cursor

    Cursor's AI features will now have access to sajn documentation.
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="VS Code">
    ### VS Code (Copilot)

    1. Create or open `.vscode/mcp.json` in your project root
    2. Add the sajn MCP server:

    ```json
    {
      "servers": {
        "sajn-docs": {
          "type": "http",
          "url": "https://docs.sajn.se/mcp"
        }
      }
    }
    ```

    3. Save the file

    GitHub Copilot will now be able to reference sajn documentation when answering questions.
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Windsurf">
    ### Windsurf

    1. Open Windsurf Settings
    2. Navigate to **Cascade** > **MCP Servers**
    3. Click **Add Server**
    4. Enter:
       - **Name**: sajn-docs
       - **URL**: `https://docs.sajn.se/mcp`
    5. Save and restart Windsurf
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Usage Tips

Once connected, you can ask your AI assistant questions about sajn:

- "How do I authenticate with the sajn API?"
- "Show me how to create a document with multiple signers"
- "What webhook events does sajn support?"
- "How do I embed the signing experience in my app?"

<Tip>
For best results, mention "sajn" in your question so the AI knows to search the sajn documentation specifically.
</Tip>

## Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="MCP server not responding">
    - Verify the URL is correct: `https://docs.sajn.se/mcp`
    - Check your internet connection
    - Try disconnecting and reconnecting the server
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="AI not using sajn documentation">
    - Make sure to mention "sajn" in your questions
    - Verify the MCP server is listed as connected in your client's settings
    - Restart your AI client after adding the MCP server
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Outdated information">
    The MCP server always serves the latest documentation. If you're seeing outdated info, the AI might be using its training data instead. Try being more specific: "Search sajn docs for..."
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Next Steps

  <Card title="Quickstart" icon="rocket" href="/quickstart">
    Get started with sajn
  <Card title="API Reference" icon="code" href="/api/introduction">
    Explore the full API

# Postman Collections

Source: https://github.com/sajn-se/sajn-docs/blob/main/postman.mdx

title: "Postman"
description: "Import ready-made Postman collections for the sajn API."

# Postman Collections

Use the Postman starter kit to make your first authenticated request, create resources, and explore the full API without building requests from scratch.

## Downloads

- [API reference collection](/downloads/postman/sajn-api-reference.postman_collection.json)
- [Getting started collection](/downloads/postman/sajn-getting-started.postman_collection.json)
- [Document lifecycle collection](/downloads/postman/sajn-document-lifecycle.postman_collection.json)
- [Contacts and signers collection](/downloads/postman/sajn-contacts-and-signers.postman_collection.json)
- [Local environment](/downloads/postman/sajn-local.postman_environment.json)

## What To Import

  <Card title="Getting Started" icon="rocket">
    Start here for auth checks, first list requests, and resource creation.
  <Card title="Document Lifecycle" icon="file-signature">
    Create a document, add a signer, send it, and fetch the signing URL.
  <Card title="Contacts & Signers" icon="users">
    Create contacts, search them, and attach them to documents.
  <Card title="API Reference" icon="code">
    Full endpoint coverage generated from the OpenAPI spec.

## Import Steps

1. Download the collections you want to use and the local environment.
2. In Postman, select **Import** and upload the JSON files.
3. Open the imported **sajn Local** environment.
4. Set `apiKey` to your API key from **Organization Settings > API Keys**.
5. Keep `baseUrl` as `https://app.sajn.se` unless you are testing against another environment.

## Built-in Variables

The starter collections use shared variables so requests chain naturally:

- `apiKey` for bearer authentication
- `baseUrl` for the main API
- `uploadBaseUrl` for file uploads
- `documentId`, `contactId`, `signerId`, `sajnIdId` for captured resource IDs

The workflow collections include test scripts that save common IDs from successful responses, so later requests can use them automatically.

## Recommended Order

1. Run **Health check** from the getting started collection.
2. Run **List all documents** or **List all contacts** to verify authentication.
3. Run **Create a new contact** and **Create a new document**.
4. Continue with the document lifecycle collection to add a signer and send the document.

## How These Collections Are Maintained

The collections are generated from our OpenAPI specification in [`api/openapi.json`](/api/introduction). When the API changes, we regenerate the files to keep request URLs, methods, and starter payloads aligned with the docs.

# Quickstart Guide

Source: https://github.com/sajn-se/sajn-docs/blob/main/quickstart.mdx

title: Quickstart
description: 'Get started with sajn in 5 minutes'

# Quickstart Guide

This guide will help you create your first document and send it for signing using the sajn API.

## Prerequisites

Before you begin, make sure you have:

- A sajn account with API access
- Your API key (found in Organization Settings > API Keys)
- A tool to make HTTP requests (cURL, Postman, or your favorite programming language)

## Step 1: Create a Contact

First, create a contact who will sign the document.

```bash
curl -X POST https://app.sajn.se/api/v1/contacts \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "firstName": "John",
    "lastName": "Doe",
    "email": "john.doe@example.com"
  }'
```

Save the returned `id` - you'll need it in the next step.

## Step 2: Create a Document

Create a new document in draft status.

```bash
curl -X POST https://app.sajn.se/api/v1/documents \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Employment Contract",
    "type": "SIGNABLE"
  }'
```

Save the returned `documentId`.

## Step 3: Add a Signer

Add your contact as a signer to the document with delivery and signature settings.

```bash
curl -X POST https://app.sajn.se/api/v1/documents/{documentId}/signers \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "contactId": "CONTACT_ID_FROM_STEP_1",
    "role": "SIGNER",
    "deliveryMethod": "EMAIL",
    "requiredSignature": "DRAWING"
  }'
```

## Step 4: Send for Signing

Send the document to the signer.

```bash
curl -X POST https://app.sajn.se/api/v1/documents/{documentId}/send \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{}'
```

That's it! The signer will receive an email with a link to sign the document (based on their `deliveryMethod` setting).
